the-bends.descriptor: "Classy dive bar" with free live music at 919 1st Ave N, since 2012

the-burg-bar-grill.text: Owner Bill Georgiou grew up in his family's Greek restaurants after they moved from Windsor, Ontario to Florida in the early 1980s and opened Grecian Gardens on Seminole Blvd, and his mother Maria's recipes still shape the menu here. That heritage is why a burger bar's signature item is a gyro feta burger.
the-burg-bar-grill.descriptor: Family-run burger pub on Central Ave, known for its gyro feta burger

the-canopy.text: The rooftop lounge on top of The Birchwood, a 1924 building that started life as the Lantern Lane Apartments, the only apartments on Beach Drive facing the bay, and later ran as Grayl's Hotel. Developer Chuck Prather bought it at a foreclosure auction, restored it, added two floors and reopened it in 2013 as a boutique hotel, with the Canopy up top giving one of downtown's best views over the waterfront and Tampa Bay.
the-canopy.descriptor: Rooftop cocktail lounge atop the Birchwood hotel on Beach Drive

the-canopy-at-birchwood.text: The rooftop lounge on top of The Birchwood, a 1924 building that started life as the Lantern Lane Apartments, the only apartments on Beach Drive facing the bay, and later ran as Grayl's Hotel. Developer Chuck Prather bought it at a foreclosure auction, restored it, added two floors and reopened it in 2013 as a boutique hotel, with the Canopy up top giving one of downtown's best views over the waterfront and Tampa Bay.
the-canopy-at-birchwood.descriptor: Rooftop cocktail lounge atop the Birchwood hotel on Beach Drive

the-chattaway.text: Built in the early 1920s as a general store, it became a sandwich-and-beer joint after Prohibition ended and is one of St. Pete's longest-lived restaurants; nobody, not even longtime owner Helen Lund, ever figured out what the name means. Lund bought it in 1951 and her family ran it for 75 years. Jillian Frers, the London-born 'Lady Chattaway' who married into the family, added the English tea room in 1999 and had the facade painted pink; 44 painted bathtubs planted with flowers ring the patio. In 2026 a group including Ferg's owner Mark Ferguson bought it to keep it open.
the-chattaway.descriptor: Pink patio sandwich-and-beer joint with an English tea room, 4th St & 22nd Ave S

the-crafty-squirrel.text: Opened in late 2018 in the old Fortunato's Italian Kitchen space on the 200 block of Central, with two industrial garage doors that roll up to the street. Owner Cameron, who grew up in the Australian outback, was so taken with squirrels on arriving in the US that he named the pub after them; inside, an exposed brick wall carries a century-old Palace Ice Cream Parlor mural.
the-crafty-squirrel.descriptor: High-energy pub and dance bar with garage doors on Central Ave, since 2018

the-dali-museum.text: Home to the largest collection of Salvador Dalí's work outside Europe, built from the private collection of Ohio industrialist A. Reynolds Morse and his wife Eleanor, who chose St. Petersburg for it in 1982. The 2011 waterfront building's free-form glass bubble, nicknamed the Enigma, nods to the geodesic dome on Dalí's own museum in Figueres, Spain.

the-don-cesar.text: The 'Pink Palace' opened in 1928, built by developer Thomas Rowe as a tribute to a lost love, and drew Jazz Age names like F. Scott Fitzgerald and Al Capone. The Army bought it in 1942 as a military hospital, the government left in 1969, and a citizens' 'Save the Don' campaign rescued it from demolition before a 1973 reopening. Hurricanes Helene and Milton forced a long closure in 2024; it reopened in March 2025.
the-don-cesar.descriptor: Pink 1928 Mediterranean-style beach resort hotel on St. Pete Beach

the-drunken-clam.text: Just across from the beach access, this orange-and-teal beach dive is known for its "naked" wings — the Cajun-Parmesan-garlic recipe took first place at the 2009 Wingstock contest among local beach bars. Look for the mural of a beer-drinking clam on the building across the street.
the-drunken-clam.descriptor: Beach dive bar off Gulf Blvd in St. Pete Beach known for naked wings

the-galley.text: Opened in late 2016 by St. Pete natives Pete Boland and Ian Taylor, who met on the St. Pete High wrestling team, in the old Reno's Downtown Joint space across from the historic open-air post office. It bills itself as a late-night steak and seafood spot, serving a full menu until 2 a.m., and every January it throws a pre-Gasparilla "Shipwrecked" party where the whole bar shows up in pirate gear.
the-galley.descriptor: Late-night tavern with steak, seafood and Cuban sandwiches at 27 4th St N

the-galley-a-st-pete-tavern.text: Opened in late 2016 by St. Pete natives Pete Boland and Ian Taylor, who met on the St. Pete High wrestling team, in the old Reno's Downtown Joint space across from the historic open-air post office. It bills itself as a late-night steak and seafood spot, serving a full menu until 2 a.m., and every January it throws a pre-Gasparilla "Shipwrecked" party where the whole bar shows up in pirate gear.
the-galley-a-st-pete-tavern.descriptor: Late-night tavern with steak, seafood and Cuban sandwiches at 27 4th St N

writtenFor.name: The Galley - A St. Pete Tavern

the-island-grille-raw-bar.descriptor: Seafood grill and raw bar with weekend breakfast on Madonna Blvd in Tierra Verde

the-james-museum.text: Opened in April 2018 by businessman Tom James and his wife Mary, who spent about $75 million turning their private collection of Western and wildlife art into a downtown museum. The building uses veined sandstone to mimic the canyons of the American Southwest, with carvings meant to evoke the Mesa Verde cliff dwellings.
the-james-museum.descriptor: Western and wildlife art museum in downtown St. Pete, opened 2018

the-oyster-bar.text: A downtown fixture on Central Avenue from 1999, taken over in 2013 by Australian restaurateur Josh Cameron and known for its oyster platters, lobster rolls and buffalo shrimp. It closed in August 2023 for what was meant to be a six-month move; the 2024 hurricane season and contractor delays stretched that to two years, and it reopened October 14, 2025 in a larger 3,200-square-foot space 20 blocks west at 2245 Central in the Grand Central District.
the-oyster-bar.descriptor: Oyster bar and seafood spot, a St. Pete fixture since 1999, now in Grand Central

the-palladium-theater.text: Built in 1925 as the First Church of Christ, Scientist, and designed by Howard Lovewell Cheney after Brunelleschi's Ospedale degli Innocenti in Florence, the building became a concert hall in 1998 and has been run by St. Petersburg College since 2007. Its century-old Skinner pipe organ was donated to a Snell Isle church in 2025 to free up stage space ahead of the theater's centennial.
the-palladium-theater.descriptor: 1925 church turned concert hall on 5th Ave N; home of Hough Hall

the-tap-room.text: The in-house restaurant of the Hollander Hotel on 4th Ave N, serving breakfast through dinner seven days a week. It's known for filet mignon, grouper nuggets and a Cuban quesadilla, plus a bakery case of pastries and cakes poured alongside locally roasted Kahwa coffee; locals get 25% off on Thursdays.
the-tap-room.descriptor: Breakfast-to-dinner restaurant and bar inside the Hollander Hotel on 4th Ave N

the-wooden-rooster.text: A downtown creperie on 2nd Ave NE whose signature savory crepe is named "The Burg" (caramelized onions, mushrooms, scrambled eggs and asiago); it grew popular enough that in 2018 it announced a second location in Seminole City Center.
the-wooden-rooster.descriptor: Breakfast-and-lunch creperie on 2nd Ave NE, downtown

thirsty-first.text: CLOSED July 26, 2026. Thirsty First opened on 1st Ave N in 2016 as a craft-cocktail lounge with lockers where regulars kept their own bottles, then grew into a sports bar and in May 2025 moved into the former Acropolis Greek Taverna building at 515 Central: nearly 9,000 square feet, two stories and 69 TVs. Owner Greg Mikurak shut it down in 2026 after a lease dispute and rising costs.
thirsty-first.descriptor: Two-story sports bar with 69 TVs at 515 Central Ave (closed 2026)

three-birds-tavern.text: The 140-year-old farmhouse, one of the original home sites in southern Pinellas County, had already housed restaurants for years when Robin and Jack King bought what was then Limey's in June 2009. Robin named it after Bob Marley's 'Three Little Birds,' a song she tied to her late mother, and the couple's restoration of the house and its towering oaks won a city beautification award in 2015; they sold to John and Haley Ruetz in 2021.
three-birds-tavern.descriptor: American tavern in a 140-year-old farmhouse on 4th St N with oak-shaded patios

tobys-original-little-italy-pizza.text: Tobia "Toby" Spinelli, a native of Naples, Italy, opened this pizzeria in the Disston Plaza shopping center in 1972, and it has stayed with the same two families ever since — a strip-mall counter-service spot that locals swear by for New York-style pies, garlic knots and a Philly cheesesteak.
tobys-original-little-italy-pizza.descriptor: New York-style pizza and subs in Disston Plaza since 1972

tonys-pizza.text: Downtown's late-night slice stop: New York-style pies sold by the slice under the tagline "Simply the Best Pizza in DTSP," with the counter open until 3 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.
tonys-pizza.descriptor: New York-style pizza by the slice on Central Ave, open late

tropicana-field.text: Opened in 1990 as the Florida Suncoast Dome before any team had signed on, it has been the Rays' home since 1998 and is MLB's only fixed-roof dome; its slanted roof and catwalk rings have famously interfered with play. Hurricane Milton shredded the roof in October 2024, sending the Rays to Tampa for all of 2025 until a nearly $60M repair brought them back for the April 2026 home opener.
tropicana-field.descriptor: Domed MLB ballpark, home of the Rays since 1998

tryst.text: Opened in spring 2016 by Paris-born Renaud Cowez, with a room designer Rob Bowen fitted out in tiled walls, a backlit onyx bar top and black lace-patterned wallpaper — a look Bowen said was inspired by lingerie. The Mediterranean-leaning menu is built around shareable plates and a French-style fruits de mer platter, and the bar stays open until 3 a.m.
tryst.descriptor: Late-night Mediterranean gastro lounge on Beach Drive across from the MFA

twin-brooks-golf-course.text: The city's nine-hole par-3 course in South St. Pete is home to First Tee St. Petersburg's junior golf program, with a driving range and a three-hole practice area for the kids; it reopened after a refurbishment covered by the Tampa Bay Times.
twin-brooks-golf-course.descriptor: City-run 9-hole par-3 course and driving range at 3800 22nd Ave S

undertow.text: A toes-in-the-sand tiki bar right on the beach at St. Pete Beach: thatched huts, volleyball nets, pool tables and frozen drinks in plastic cups. Its quirk is a "rubber duck river" that flows around the bar, and I Love the Burg has called it one of the most scenic beach bars in America.
undertow.descriptor: Open-air tiki beach bar on the sand at 3850 Gulf Blvd, St. Pete Beach

valentys-lounge.text: Tucked behind Pasadena Liquors, Valenty's is a time capsule: the interior copies a kiosk bar that founder John Valenty saw at the Pittsburgh airport, and his son Jim, a former elementary school teacher, has run it since 1990 with the original furniture, a piano, free popcorn, $2 beers and a house whiskey old fashioned.
valentys-lounge.descriptor: Family-run cocktail lounge behind a liquor store, known for cheap old fashioneds

vinoy-park.text: This 11.6-acre stretch of downtown waterfront takes its name from the neighboring Vinoy Park Hotel, built in 1925. It is the city's go-to outdoor event lawn, hosting the Tampa Bay Blues Festival, Ribfest, concerts, art festivals and triathlons.
vinoy-park.descriptor: Downtown waterfront park and festival lawn beside the Vinoy hotel

webbs-city-cellar.text: Green Bench Brewing's second tasting room, opened in 2019 next to the brewery on Baum Ave, is named for Webb's City, Doc Webb's self-styled "World's Most Unusual Drug Store" that sprawled across downtown St. Pete from 1926 to 1979 with 77 departments and in-store sideshows. The climate-controlled cellar holds up to 700 wine barrels of sour and wild ales, plus house mead and cider.
webbs-city-cellar.descriptor: Green Bench's barrel-aged sour, mead and cider tasting room on Baum Ave, since 2019

wharf-seafood-restaurant.text: A Pass-a-Grille fixture for more than 30 years, housed in a roughly century-old building on the bayside where boaters tie up at the docks. The blackened grouper sandwich is the calling card the place is famous for, and there's live music on the front porch Wednesday through Saturday.
wharf-seafood-restaurant.descriptor: Bayside seafood spot on Pass-a-Grille Way known for its blackened grouper sandwich

wild-child.text: Opened in summer 2020 in the former NuMex space by St. Pete natives Matt Kaye (also behind The Bends) and chef Rob Reinsmith, who came home after years in New York restaurants. The menu borrows from Tulum, the Caribbean and beyond — jerk octopus, snapper ceviche, a Korean fried chicken sandwich — under murals by local and Miami artists.
wild-child.descriptor: Tropical-leaning neighborhood bistro and cocktail bar on Central Ave in Grand Central

williams-park.text: St. Petersburg's first park, laid out in 1888 as City Park and renamed for city co-founder John C. Williams; it fills a whole downtown block between 3rd and 4th Streets. A bandstand has stood here since 1894 - the current bandshell, designed by local architect William B. Harvard in 1954, won an AIA Award of Merit the next year - and in 1964 Richard Nixon used it to stump for Barry Goldwater.
williams-park.descriptor: Downtown's original city-block park with a 1954 bandshell, 4th St N at 2nd Ave N

woodson-african-american-museum.text: Housed in a former administrative office of Jordan Park, St. Petersburg's first Black public housing community, the museum opened in 2006 after a 1997 HUD Hope VI grant rebuilt the neighborhood. Local schoolchildren chose to name it for Carter G. Woodson, the historian who helped establish Black History Month. It rebranded as the Woodson African American Museum of Florida in 2021 and launched a capital campaign for a larger purpose-built home.
woodson-african-american-museum.descriptor: African American history and art museum in a former Jordan Park office building

zom-hee-chinese-restaurant.text: Family-owned since 1985 in Seminole's Park Place Center on Park Blvd, Zom Hee cooks Szechuan, Hunan and Cantonese dishes in a 250-seat dining room with a cocktail lounge pouring Mai Tais, Blue Hawaiis and a house drink called the Confucius Itch.
zom-hee-chinese-restaurant.descriptor: Family-run Szechuan/Hunan/Cantonese restaurant on Park Blvd in Seminole since 1985
